tasks.corrected_reference_answer: raise_catch_raise catches and prints the original exception, then raises a fresh Exception from None (tests/functional/b/broad_exception/broad_exception_raised.py:33-38). This explicitly suppresses display of implicit exception context; it does not delete the stored context. In the AST, explicit from None supplies a cause node, so visit_raise routes to _check_bad_exception_cause, which accepts a Const whose value is None (pylint/checkers/exceptions.py:319-373). The broad-exception-raised warning remains applicable to the newly raised generic Exception.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Caching associates a call key with a retained result, permitting repeated equivalent calls to reuse that result. On instance methods, the key includes the instance. Pylint identifies functools.cache and lru_cache(maxsize=None) and emits method-cache-max-size-none, with exemptions for enum ancestry and non-instance methods (pylint/checkers/stdlib.py:726-766). An unbounded cache can retain arguments and results while entries remain cached; clearing or discarding the cache can release those references. The source does not imply a reverse result-to-argument mapping.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: MyString is a minimal lint fixture: rjust only calls width.__index__ and returns no formatted string (tests/functional/u/unnecessary/unnecessary_dunder_call.py:127-131). A proposed production design should retain str inheritance and delegate formatting and built-in argument validation to super().rjust(width, fillchar), returning its result. If extra domain validation is required, put it in a helper before delegation and document any stricter behavior. No __init__ override or mutable validator instance is necessary. This proposal restores built-in formatting semantics; it is not behavior-preserving for the existing fixture.
